title: By-law dispatch, inclusionary zoning and heritage rebates
subtitle: Immigration Waterloo Region funding deferred, OMERS pension changes, urban design manual launch, and two development applications reviewed
overview: Council endorsed a dedicated by-law dispatch operation shared with neighbouring municipalities, starting July 1, 2026. Waterloo's estimated annual contribution of $260,000 will be considered in the 2027 operating budget. Council also approved an inclusionary zoning framework and directed staff to prepare the matching zoning by-law amendment, so a share of new housing units will have to be affordable.

On heritage, council asked staff to continue the Municipal Heritage Register Review and to refer a property tax rebate program (Option B) to the 2027 budget process. Staff will also reach out to owners of properties on the heritage registry by the end of Q2 2026. Council approved Waterloo's participation in the OMERS pension plan for members of Council from the next term, and opposed the provincial changes to OMERS governance in Bill 68.

A funding request from Immigration Waterloo Region was deferred so the organization can attend and answer questions {{vote:m8}}. Council also received the Urban Design Manual 2.0 launch report and held informal public meetings on two development applications, at 41 Westhill Drive and on Seagram Drive. No decisions were made on those.

decisions.detail: Council endorsed a shared dispatch model starting July 1, 2026, directed staff to include an estimated $260,000 annual city contribution in the 2027 operating budget, and authorized the CAO to sign the agreement.
Council approved the Inclusionary Zoning By-law Amendment Framework and directed staff to advance a zoning by-law amendment to implement it.
Council directed staff to continue the heritage register review, refer Option B rebates to the 2027 budget process, and conduct outreach to registry property owners by the end of Q2 2026.
Council deferred the funding request to the February 23, 2026 meeting, or the next meeting the organization can attend, to get clarification {{vote:m8}}.
Council approved participation in the OMERS Primary Pension Plan and its Retirement Compensation Arrangement for Members of Council, effective with the next term on November 15, 2026.

decisions.item: Opposition to OMERS changes in Bill 68
decisions.detail: Council resolved not to support the Bill 68 changes to OMERS governance, asked the province to reconsider, and backed AMO's call to keep the two-board model.
Council received the staff report launching the update of the Urban Design Manual for information.

debate: On by-law dispatch, one councillor accepted the need to keep enforcement staff safe but questioned why a 24/7 police-run dispatch is needed when it has handled only noise and nuisance calls. The councillor asked staff to look at non-police alternatives and flagged the new cost for public attention. Staff said parking calls would stay separate and that budget increases would go through the budget process.

On inclusionary zoning, staff argued that setting a firm start date gives the industry certainty, because no ideal market moment will come. A councillor said the development industry's preferred time is never, and voiced disappointment at the slow pace and at provincial changes.

On heritage rebates, a delegate supported a program and worried about the register being reset at the start of 2027. Some councillors worried the rebates could be a wealth transfer to owners of heritage properties and wanted to know the cost. Staff said the referral would not commit the 2027 budget and that it would at least appear on the menu list.

On the Immigration Waterloo Region request, councillors regretted that no representative was present to answer questions and sought a deferral. Others noted that the request would mainly fund staffing, which the city does not normally fund, and cited past requests from other organizations that council did not support.

At the development meetings, councillors raised traffic and pedestrian crossing concerns near Westhill Drive, light and wind effects, shadow studies, and water conservation. A resident delegate asked about stadium noise, wind effects on athletes, and energy and refuge-area features for the Seagram Drive proposal.
